I will keep my full 7.7 mu in the wheat-maize rotation because I already know this system, I have well irrigation, and after only 2 years of farming I would rather stay with a simple and familiar plan than take risks. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put in moderate fertilizer, irrigate a few times, and manage weeds and disease with a small number of pesticide sprays, because wheat here needs steady water and nutrition to give me a stable yield. After wheat harvest, I will plant hybrid maize on the same 7.7 mu, because hybrid maize fits my goal of getting a reliable output from limited land; I will use a bit more nitrogen than wheat, keep phosphorus and potassium moderate, irrigate when needed through the well, and do a few pesticide applications for weeds and insects. Since some family labor is off-farm, I will keep management practical and not overly intensive, using rotary tillage because it is easier for me to organize and suits this double-cropping system.
